**Instructions.** Choose the single best answer (a–e) for each question. You may use a periodic table.
Calculators are allowed. Answers are rounded to the precision shown. Time yourself: aim for about 30 minutes
(roughly 2 minutes per question, the same pace as the full exam). The strong-acid and strong-base lists are **not** provided: work from memory.

**Answer sheet.** Use the bubble answer sheet (`CHEM1301/exam-prep/answer-sheet/answer-sheet.pdf`), rows 1–15.

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**1.** According to the Arrhenius definition used in this course, a **base** is a substance that:

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ loses electrons to a nonmetal\
b)\ produces H^+^ ions when it is dissolved in water\
c)\ always contains a metal\
d)\ is always insoluble in water\
e)\ produces hydroxide ions (OH^−^) when it is dissolved in water

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ KOH\
b)\ Fe(OH)~3~\
c)\ HCl\
d)\ NH~3~\
e)\ Mg(OH)~2~

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

**3.** What **salt** forms when nitric acid reacts completely with calcium hydroxide? 2HNO~3~(aq) + Ca(OH)~2~(aq) $\rightarrow$ ? + 2H~2~O(l)

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ CaNO~3~\
b)\ H~2~O\
c)\ Ca~2~NO~3~\
d)\ Ca(NO~3~)~2~\
e)\ Ca(OH)~2~

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**4.** Sulfuric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide: H~2~SO~4~(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) $\rightarrow$ Na~2~SO~4~(aq) + 2H~2~O(l). What is the **net ionic** equation (smallest whole-number coefficients)?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ H^+^(aq) + OH^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ H~2~O(l)\
b)\ 2H^+^(aq) + SO~4~^2−^(aq) + 2Na^+^(aq) + 2OH^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ 2Na^+^(aq) + SO~4~^2−^(aq) + 2H~2~O(l)\
c)\ H~2~SO~4~(aq) + 2OH^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ SO~4~^2−^(aq) + 2H~2~O(l)\
d)\ 2Na^+^(aq) + SO~4~^2−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ Na~2~SO~4~(s)\
e)\ 2H^+^(aq) + 2OH^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ 2H~2~O(l)

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**5.** When the equation below is balanced with the smallest whole-number coefficients, what is the **sum** of all four coefficients?

\_\_ H~3~PO~4~(aq) + \_\_ KOH(aq) $\rightarrow$ \_\_ K~3~PO~4~(aq) + \_\_ H~2~O(l)

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 4\
b)\ 6\
c)\ 8\
d)\ 10\
e)\ 12

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**6.** Which reaction is **not** an oxidation–reduction reaction?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Zn(s) + 2HCl(aq) $\rightarrow$ ZnCl~2~(aq) + H~2~(g)\
b)\ Pb(NO~3~)~2~(aq) + 2NaCl(aq) $\rightarrow$ PbCl~2~(s) + 2NaNO~3~(aq)\
c)\ 2Na(s) + Cl~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ 2NaCl(s)\
d)\ N~2~(g) + O~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ 2NO(g)\
e)\ CH~4~(g) + 2O~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ CO~2~(g) + 2H~2~O(g)

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**7.** In the reaction 3Ca(s) + N~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ Ca~3~N~2~(s), how many electrons does **each nitrogen atom** gain?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 1\
b)\ 2\
c)\ 3\
d)\ 5\
e)\ 6

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

**8.** For Cu(s) + 2AgNO~3~(aq) $\rightarrow$ Cu(NO~3~)~2~(aq) + 2Ag(s), which statement is correct?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Each Cu atom loses 2 electrons and each Ag^+^ ion gains 2 electrons\
b)\ Each Cu atom gains 2 electrons\
c)\ The NO~3~^−^ ions transfer electrons to silver\
d)\ No electrons transfer; the anions simply swap partners\
e)\ Each Cu atom loses 2 electrons and each Ag^+^ ion gains 1 electron

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**9.** According to the course, what happens when a **metal** reacts with a **nonmetal**?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ The nonmetal transfers electrons to the metal\
b)\ An ionic compound forms as the metal transfers electrons to the nonmetal, so the reaction is always redox\
c)\ A molecular (non-ionic) compound forms by sharing electrons\
d)\ No electrons transfer, so it is classified as a synthesis only\
e)\ It is redox only if O~2~ is one of the reactants

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

b)\ decomposition\
c)\ precipitation\
d)\ double-displacement\

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

**12.** Methane burns in a gas stove: CH~4~(g) + 2O~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ CO~2~(g) + 2H~2~O(g). Which classes apply?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ combustion only\
b)\ decomposition and oxidation–reduction\
c)\ synthesis and combustion\
d)\ acid–base, because water is a product\
e)\ combustion and oxidation–reduction

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

**13.** According to the course, a **single-replacement** reaction is one in which:

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ a single substance reacts with oxygen\
b)\ a single compound breaks into two elements\
c)\ no electrons are transferred\
d)\ a single type of anion is exchanged between two cations, as Cl^−^ moves from H^+^ to Zn^2+^ in Zn + 2HCl\
e)\ two anions exchange cation partners

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```
